transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sophie Miller (Redwood AE), Carlos Vega (Redwood SE), Lina Ortiz (Redwood CSM) — Dana Patel (Nebula VP Eng), Evan Cho (Nebula Platform Lead), Mira Zhang (Nebula Data Ops), Samir Khan (Nebula Security), Priya Rao (Nebula Product)

Summary: quick Q3 health sync focused on unexpected cost bump in August, two short incidents in last month, and alignment on pilot -> dedicated roll criteria. Agreed to run performance bench, share traffic histograms, and push security artifacts.

[00:00] Sophie Miller: hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh we thought today we'd do a quick health sync — usage, cost, reliability, then roadmap items for the q4 pilot. how's that sound?
[00:10] Dana Patel: yep that works, we've got a few folks on from infra and security. thanks for setting this up.
[00:18] Carlos Vega: cool, i'll jump into the perf bits when we get to incidents, i've pulled some logs and traces but might need the nebula sample to run a fair bench.
[00:27] Evan Cho: question up front — you said cost bump in august, can you summarize? was that token-level, repeat inference, or something else?
[00:36] Lina Ortiz: i'll take the billing side — we saw a usage spike around Aug 10–13, there were a lot of repeated shorter sequences and some cache misses, which combined with a small config change on batching led to a 22% increase week-over-week.
[00:53] Mira Zhang: yeah we had a launch of a new alerting rule that triggered many backfills; that created fanout to the model endpoints, my bad. we didn't anticipate the kv cache invalidation.
[01:04] Sophie Miller: no worries, these things happen. main thing — do we have a guardrail so this doesn't recur? some quick knobs: prefix caching, TTLs, and a staging rule that throttles backfills.
[01:18] Dana Patel: can Redwood detect and fallback to a cheaper variant automatically if we exceed budget or SLOs?
[01:25] Carlos Vega: yes — we have routing policies that can route to quantized variants or smaller context models when latency or cost policies hit thresholds. i can show the policy config; it's pretty straightforward.
[01:38] Evan Cho: is that available on private? our compliance team prefers VPC-only traffic.
[01:45] Sophie Miller: totally; dedicated and private modes support the same runtime policies. the only difference is the control plane for private — your controlplane will be in your VPC and we can configure peering.
[01:55] Samir Khan: on peering — we need details on KMS integration and whether tokens or raw payloads ever touch Redwood-managed storage.
[02:04] Lina Ortiz: we'll share the network diagram and SOC2 packet after the call. redwood doesn't persist raw payloads for the pilot if you set retention to zero, and KMS can be customer-managed in our private option.

Topics: Usage spike root cause, Incident review x2 (Aug 12 & Sep 02), Pilot -> Dedicated gating, Security and VPC/KMS, Q4 rollout timeline.

[07:10] Carlos Vega: i want to walk through the two incidents quickly. Aug 12 — we saw a KV cache miss storm; the pattern was many short requests with different prefixes causing the cache to thrash and higher token regen. latency spiked to ~480 ms p95 for 30 minutes. the second, Sep 02, was a degraded GPU kernel due to a driver mismatch during an autoscaler event — short outage, fallback served on CPU with higher latency.
[07:45] Dana Patel: can we get the exact p50/p95 numbers and which model families were impacted? we need that in our postmortem with execs.
[07:55] Carlos Vega: sure — augmenting quickly: Aug 12 p95 went from 220ms baseline to 480ms, p99 to ~1.1s. the model was a 7B open family variant; Sep 02 saw p95 zone-level increase to 750ms while fallback served — we have logs we'll share.
[08:16] Mira Zhang: the driver mismatch — was that on Redwood's infra or ours?
[08:20] Carlos Vega: that was on the Dedicated pool controller during a node replacement; we patched the autoscaler config to pin driver versions. not a customer-side misconfig.
[08:28] Samir Khan: ok we'll note that.

[12:02] Evan Cho: about the pilot -> dedicated gating: what metrics do you recommend? SLOs, cost per 1M tokens, error rate thresholds?
[12:11] Sophie Miller: recommended gates: sustained p95 < 300ms for two weeks, error rate < 0.2% (5xx and timeouts), predictable cost delta per 1M tokens under reserved vs hosted, and load test with traffic multiplier x3. we also want to verify model equivalence for output quality on sample prompts.
[12:34] Priya Rao: for product, the quality equivalence is key. we ran A/B on a small set and saw slight diff on edge cases — is that expected between quantized and full fp16?
[12:44] Carlos Vega: yes small variation is expected; we provide eval tooling and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. we can run your prompts through both variants and provide a diff report.

[18:05] Mira Zhang: for the perf bench, what do you need from us?
[18:09] Carlos Vega: ideally — a sample of 1k representative requests with timestamps and context lengths, plus a traffic profile distribution (p10/p50/p90 context lengths), plus the top 10 endpoints by traffic. that lets us mimic real workload for batching and caching config.
[18:25] Dana Patel: we can extract that; i'll own it. expect the histogram by friday.

[23:40] Sophie Miller: quick note on cost controls — there's an "autosubmit budget" guard that can block large background jobs and send an alert to your admins; also token caps per API key.
[23:52] Evan Cho: would that have stopped our backfill? possibly, yes. can we test that on staging?
[23:58] Lina Ortiz: yep we'll help set a staging policy that throttles backfill jobs under a named tag so you can simulate.

[29:10] Samir Khan: security questions — we need details on audit logs retention, field-level encryption, and SSO integration.
[29:18] Lina Ortiz: audit logs can be exported to your SIEM via secure forwarder, retention is configurable. field-level encryption is available in private mode. SSO/SAML is supported; we can share the SAML metadata.
[29:30] Samir Khan: perfect, please send the packet.

[34:00] Carlos Vega: i'll propose a performance plan — step 1 run bench and adjust continuous batching parameters; step 2 tune KV cache TTL; step 3 re-run to ensure p95 under threshold. the bench will show where autoscaling vs pooling helps.
[34:18] Dana Patel: curious — will pooling help with sudden fanout vs autoscaler?
[34:22] Carlos Vega: pooling gives warm KV caches and faster cold-start behavior; autoscaler complements it for throughput. for your backfills a staging pool with higher cache TTL may be the sweet spot.

[40:05] Priya Rao: timeline: we want to start limited pilot for a feature flag rollout mid-october. is that doable?
[40:13] Sophie Miller: yes — mid-oct pilot is feasible. next steps before then: bench, security docs, pilot pricing and contract, and a final go/no-go 1 week before.
[40:25] Dana Patel: any blockers from Redwood side?
[40:28] Sophie Miller: nothing blocking — just need traffic sample and confirmation on KMS peering for private pilot.

[46:00] Carlos Vega: one other note — we noticed some mismatched model artifacts in your staging bucket that caused a fallback; nothing critical but you'll want to coordinate model pushes via the onboarding API so we can validate hashes.
[46:16] Mira Zhang: good catch; we'll standardize the pipeline.

[48:40] Sophie Miller: recap: action items assigned — we will send SOC2 packet, bench plan, and pilot pricing. client to send traffic histograms and KMS requirements. schedule follow-up 2026-09-29 to review bench results and finalize pilot contract.
[48:58] Dana Patel: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[49:05] Priya Rao: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[49:12] Samir Khan: we'll review security docs and get back with notes.
[49:20] Carlos Vega: i'll kick off bench once i have the sample — expect an initial report within 3 business days of receiving data.
[49:30] Sophie Miller: great — i'll send the materials this afternoon. thanks all.

End of transcript.
